frames.evidence: The vector search paper defines recall at ten and compares lexical retrieval with dense embeddings on developer documentation.
The evaluation paper explains that a held out benchmark avoids tuning retrieval thresholds directly on reported results.
The paper's methods section measures ranking quality with labeled query and document pairs instead of anecdotal search examples.
The release checklist tracks signed builds, changelog review, smoke tests, and the owner approval needed before publishing.
The checklist records the QA pass, rollback notes, and deployment owner for the next desktop release candidate.
The release note draft links smoke evidence and says no production rollout happens before a human visual check.
Returning to the vector search paper, the conclusion recommends tracking false positives alongside recall during retrieval changes.
The vector evaluation appendix documents pairwise labels and a reproducible scoring script for the benchmark corpus.
